 Sallie Mae (SLM) Stock Fair Value Edges Lower After Analysts Cut Targets
 Sasha Jovanovic Sun, November 8, 2026 at 2:06 AM EST 3 min read SLM -3.34%

 Learn more The latest update for Sallie Mae points to a lower assessed fair value, moving from US$26.09 to US$24.78 per share. This reset lines up with recent analyst commentary that highlights a mixed picture, with reduced price targets alongside ongoing confidence in SLM's ability to execute over time despite recent earnings pressure and credit concerns. Read on to see how these shifting targets, and the debate behind them, can help you track the evolving narrative around SLM. 
 Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value SLM. 
 What Wall Street Has Been Saying 
 🐂 Bullish Takeaways 
 Several firms, including TD Cowen, RBC Capital, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo, still carry positive ratings on SLM despite trimming price targets. That signals continued confidence in SLM's long term execution. 
 RBC Capital highlights SLM's progress in pivoting its model toward expanded loan volumes and a new forward flow partner, which the firm says can support more consistent fee income over time. 
 Morgan Stanley recently upgraded SLM to Overweight and pointed to capital light private credit partnerships as a potential earnings driver once macro and rate pressures ease. 
 🐻 Bearish Takeaways 
 TD Cowen points to a broad based 3Q loss for SLM, driven in part by higher provisions tied to smaller loan sales and lower gains on sale, which has led to a lower US$27 price target. 
 Wells Fargo and Barclays both cut price targets, with Wells citing market volatility and delayed seasoned loan sales that fed into lower 2026 EPS guidance, and ongoing debt resolution issues that are still weighing on the story.

 How This Changes the Fair Value For SLM 
 Fair value has moved from US$26.09 to US$24.78 per share. 
 Revenue growth assumptions have adjusted from 61.89% to 56.68%. 
 Net profit margin is broadly similar, moving from 41.50% to 41.64%. 
 Future P/E has shifted from 8.39x to 8.11x. 
 The discount rate used in models has changed from 11.04% to 11.79%.
